messages.subject: lavaan interaction and mediation effects
parts:
Dear all, I know that this is a popular topic and there are some useful blogs (very few) on this topic. I have three latent factors, say F1 and F2, F3 which are also correlated. F1 has two indicators and F2 has three and F3 has two. 
DV1 and DV2 are two dependent variables. However, DV2, is a mediator variable, that is, F1 and F2 are independent latent factors for both DV2 and DV1, but DV2 is also an independent variable for DV1. I believe that there is an interaction between F1 and DV2, when predicting DV1. This is the solution I gave

model00 <- '
F1 =~ v1 + v2
F2 =~ v3 + v4 + v5
F3 =~ v6 + v7
Interaction.F1.DV2  =~ inter.v1 + inter.v2 
DV2 ~ F1 + F2 + F3
DV1 ~ F1 + F2 + F3 + DV2 + Interaction.F1.DV2
'
inter.v1 <- v1 * DV2 
inter.v2 <- v2 * DV2

Does this make sense? Could anyone suggest an "easy" reading regarding the interpretation?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan interaction and mediation effects
parts:
I'd suggest using the residual-centering approach.  Check the semTools::indProd() function, and the help page has 3 references (the Little et al., 2006, reference is readable, although the method is tedious enough that you might need to read through it a couple times).

Terry
